Once those were Aspirations, 
Now they are Ambitions of 
a Future, Fully Made in Bharat
India is entering one of the most deﬁning chapters in its 
history. Driven by the vision of Viksit Bharat and 
Aatmanirbhar Bharat, the nation is accelerating towards 
becoming a global leader in manufacturing, clean energy , 
advanced technologies and industrial innovation. At the 
heart of this transformation lies a strategic imperative: 
securing the natural resources that make sustainable 
growth possible .
For over six decades, GMDC has proudly contributed to this 
national journey . As India 's leading Mining PSU, we have 
transformed the nation 's mineral wealth into the energy , 
resources and capabilities that power industries, 
strengthen infrastructure and support economic progress. 
Today , our role extends far beyond mining. Through our 
expanding presence in coal, critical minerals, renewable 
energy , Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation and value-added 
mineral ecosystems, we are helping build the foundations 
of India 's next era of growth.
As the nation advances towards greater self-reliance and 
global competitiveness, GMDC remains committed to 
catalysing national priorities. From mining the resources 
that India needs, to making the capabilities that India 
demands, to fulﬁlling the aspirations of a nation on the rise, 
we’re committed towards  Enabling Billion Dreams of 
Viksit Bharat.
=== page 5 ===
GMDC At a Glance 
Enabling Bharat’s Growth Evolution
Evolution is driven by the ability to adapt, innovate and 
grow with changing times. For India, it reﬂects a deﬁning 
national shift towards self-reliance, technological 
leadership and the conﬁdence to build a future powered by 
its own resources, capabilities and enterprise . As the nation 
advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, 
strategic natural resources are becoming increasingly 
central to manufacturing excellence , energy security and 
economic resilience. It is within this evolving national 
landscape that GMDC has continually transformed itself 
over the past six decades. Today , as one of India 's leading 
Mining PSUs, the Company is building a diversiﬁed 
portfolio of strategic mineral and energy assets that not 
only addresses the needs of the present but also enables 
the ambitions of a future-ready India. From its expanding lignite operations across Gujarat that 
continue to strengthen the state' s industrial and energy 
ecosystem, to its three coal assets in Odisha that reinforce 
India's long-term energy security, GMDC remains 
committed to developing the resources that power the 
nation. The Company is also advancing the Ambaji Copper 
Project and the Ambadungar R are Earth Elements Project, 
securing minerals that are indispensable for electric 
mobility , renewable energy , advanced electronics, defence 
technologies and next-generation manufacturing.
Beyond conventional mining, GMDC is pioneering 
Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation (UCG) projects at EFG Valia 
and Ghala in Gujarat, with another project progressing at 
Burapahar in Odisha. By converting deep coal reserves into 
cleaner synthesis gas, UCG has the potential to create an Enabling Billion Dreams of Viksit Bharat

Enabling Billion Dreams of Viksit Bharat
8Chairman’s Desk 
Dear Stakeholders,
As we reﬂect on another year in GMDC' s journey , I do so 
with a deep sense of conﬁdence in the direction our 
Company is taking and gratitude for the trust placed in us 
by our stakeholders. The year has been one of meaningful 
progress, shaped not only by strong operational and 
ﬁnancial performance but also by a clear strategic vision to 
strengthen GMDC' s role in India 's long-term development.
Advancing the Viksit Bharat @2047 Vision
India today stands at a deﬁning moment in its development 
journey . The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents far 
more than economic growth. It reﬂects the nation 's 
aspiration to build resilient supply chains, strengthen 
domestic manufacturing, accelerate technological 
capability and secure the strategic resources that will 
power the next generation of progress. As the global 
economy undergoes profound transformation, resource 
security has emerged as an essential pillar of national 
resilience . Organisations such as GMDC therefore have an 
increasingly important role to play in shaping India 's future .
Strengthening National Presence
Over more than six decades, GMDC has evolved from a 
state mining company into one of India 's leading Mining 
PSUs. While Gujarat remains the foundation of our success, 
the Company' s contribution today extends well beyond 
state boundaries. By supporting energy security , enabling 
industrial development and strengthening self-reliance in 
strategic resources, GMDC is steadily expanding its role as 
a national institution committed to creating enduring value 
for the country .
Powering India 's Energy Future
Energy remains fundamental to national development, and 
GMDC continues to play an important role in strengthening 
that foundation. Our expanding lignite operations across 
Gujarat continue to support industries and MSMEs that 
drive the state' s economy , while our growing presence in 
Odisha represents the next chapter of the Company' s 
evolution. The development of our coal assets in the state 
reﬂects a long-term commitment to strengthening India 's 
energy security while creating new opportunities for 
employment, regional development and inclusive 
economic growth. Gujarat will always remain the heart of 
GMDC' s journey , while Odisha represents the Company' s 
future as a truly multi-state mining enterprise .
Unlocking India 's Strategic Mineral Potential
The future , however , will be shaped not only by energy 
resources but also by the strategic minerals that enable 
modern economies.      As India accelerates its 
transition towards advanced 
manufacturing, clean 
energy , electric mobility and 
emerging technologies, 
access to critical minerals 
has become increasingly 
important. GMDC is 
responding to this national 
priority by steadily building 
capabilities across Copper , 
Rare Earth Elements and 
other strategic resources 
that will strengthen domestic 
value chains, reduce import 
dependence and support 
India 's growing 
technological and industrial 
aspirations. 
These investments reﬂect our conviction that resource 
security and economic self-reliance are inseparable .
Building Capabilities for Tomorrow
Equally important is our commitment to building an 
organisation that is prepared for the future . Digital 
technologies, innovation and responsible mining practices 
are becoming integral to the way GMDC creates value . 
Alongside these eﬀorts, the Company continues to invest 
in institutional capability through its specialised societies, 
research initiatives and leadership development 
programmes, strengthening the knowledge ecosystem 
that will support innovation, exploration and organisational 
excellence for years to come .
=== page 10 ===
Towards Creating Shared Prosperity
Growth at GMDC has always been guided by a broader 
sense of purpose . Through Gramya Vikas Trust, we 
continue to invest in education, healthcare , skill 
development, livelihood creation and community 
infrastructure across Gujarat and Odisha. These initiatives 
are not viewed as obligations, but as an integral part of the 
Company' s identity and its enduring commitment to 
inclusive development.
I convey my sincere appreciation to the Government of 
Gujarat, the Government of India, my colleagues on the 
Board, the management team, employees, shareholders, 
customers, business partners and the communities around 
our operations for their continued trust and support. Their 
conﬁdence inspires us to remain steadfast in our purpose 
and ambitious in our vision for the future .Warm regards,
Dr. Hasmukh Adhia, IA S (Retd.)
Chairman, GMDC

Managing Director’s Desk Enabling Billion Dreams of Viksit Bharat
10Dear Stakeholders,
History has shown that every deﬁning chapter of human 
progress has been shaped by the resources that powered 
it. Coal powered the Industrial Revolution. Oil fuelled the 
modern economy . Today , the world stands at the threshold 
of another such chapter . As economies transition towards 
cleaner energy , technology-led growth, strategic minerals 
and energy resources are becoming central to economic 
resilience and long-term prosperity .
Advancing India ’s Resource Security
India has embraced this transition with remarkable speed 
and strategic foresight. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 is 
built upon strengthening domestic manufacturing, 
securing critical supply chains, accelerating technological 
capability and creating an economy that is increasingly 
powered by its own resources and enterprise . As one of 
India's leading Mining PSUs, GMDC has a unique 
responsibility in helping realise this national aspiration.
The past year has been one of disciplined execution and 
purposeful transformation. We delivered one of the 
strongest ﬁnancial performances in the Company' s history , 
recording our second-highest Proﬁt Before Tax of 
₹1,302 crore , while continuing to invest in strategic assets 
and future-oriented businesses. These achievements 
reaﬃrm the strength of our operating model and provide us 
with the conﬁdence to pursue opportunities that will deﬁne 
the next phase of GMDC' s growth.
Strengthening Our Commitment T owards Gujarat' s 
Energy Growth
For over four decades, lignite has remained the 
cornerstone of our business and an enduring contributor to 
Gujarat' s industrial development. Today , our ﬁve operating 
lignite mines, together with ﬁve upcoming projects holding 
reserves exceeding 300 million tonnes, continue to 
support thousands of MSMEs and industries by providing 
dependable domestic fuel. As we increase our production 
capacity from 8 MTPA to 10 MTPA, we are reinforcing the 
state' s industrial ecosystem while strengthening India 's 
long-term energy security .
Expanding into New Growth Frontiers
Our expansion into Odisha marks one of the most 
signiﬁcant milestones in the Company' s evolution. With 
three commercial coal assets encompassing nearly 
2 billion tonnes of geological resources, GMDC is 
establishing a strong presence in one of India 's richest coal-
bearing regions.
At the centre of this portfolio is the Baitarni West Mine , 
envisioned with a peak production capacity of 15 MTPA and 
poised to become one of India 's largest Tier-III commercial 
coal mines. These assets represent far more than 
geographical expansion. They establish Odisha as GMDC' s 
next major growth engine while creating employment, 
strengthening regional infrastructure and contributing to 
the long-term economic development of the state .Pioneering New Pathways for Resource Utilisation
Innovation remains fundamental to our growth strategy . 
Through Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation (UCG) projects at 
EFG Valia and Ghala in Gujarat and Burapahar in Odisha, 
GMDC is pioneering cleaner pathways for unlocking deep 
coal reserves that have traditionally remained inaccessible . 
Beyond enhancing resource utilisation, these initiatives 
have the potential to support downstream industries 
through the production of syngas for methanol, ammonia, 
fertilisers and speciality chemicals.
Advancing Towards India ’s Next-gen Mineral Ecosystem
As India 's industrial ambitions continue to evolve , so too 
must the nation's resource base. The future will 
increasingly be shaped by minerals that enable 
electriﬁcation, renewable energy , advanced electronics 
and strategic technologies. Recognising this shift, GMDC is 
building an integrated portfolio that positions the Company 
at the forefront of India's emerging critical mineral 
ecosystem.
Our USD 2.5 billion Copper Project at Ambaji, with 
appro ximately 10 million tonnes of identiﬁed Copper along 
with other base metals, will strengthen domestic Copper 
availability for power infrastructure, electric mobility, 
renewable energy and advanced manufacturing.
Equally signiﬁcant is our Ambadungar Rare Earth Elements 
Project, where we are laying the foundation for the Bharat 
Rare Earth Ecosystem. With a planned ore production 
capacity of 1.6 MTPA, the project is envisioned as an 
integrated value chain encompassing extraction, 
beneﬁciation, separation, processing and downstream 
manufacturing within India. The Ambadungar Rare Earth 
Elements Project is an important step towards building 
India ’s own rare earth ecosystem, strengthening domestic 
capabilities and advancing the nation ’s technological and 
industrial self-reliance .
It is a strategic investment in India's technological 
sovereignty and future industrial competitiveness.    Odisha represents a new 
chapter for GMDC, both in 
strengthening our resource 
base and contributing to 
India ’s long-term energy 
security . As we grow in the 
State, we also look forward 
to creating opportunities, 
strengthening infrastructure 
and contributing to Odisha ’s 
economic progress.
=== page 12 ===
Driving Digital Transformation
Building a future-ready organisation requires more than 
expanding assets. It demands new ways of operating. 
Guided by our vision of achieving fourfold growth by 2030 , 
GMDC is undertaking a focussed digital transformation 
centred on high-impact technology investments that 
deliver measurable business outcomes. Strengthening 
connectivity across remote mining sites has laid the 
foundation for IoT and real-time operational intelligence . 
IoT-enabled equipment monitoring has reduced production 
costs by nearly 10%, while digital initiatives across land 
management, customer services and logistics have 
enhanced transparency and improved operational 
eﬃciency. With an AI-enabled Command and Control 
Centre under development, GMDC is creating an 
integrated digital ecosystem that will enhance mine 
planning, operational safety, resource utilisation and 
enterprise-wide decision-making as the Company scales 
towards its long-term growth ambitions.
Building Resilient Institutional Capability
Building future-ready capability extends beyond 
technology integration and towards creating knowledge 
ecosystems that will sustain innovation and prepare the 
organisation for the opportunities of tomorrow . GMDC, 
through its specialised vehicles, is bringing together 
innovation, exploration and leadership development into a 
cohesive ecosystem of capability building. The 
International Center of Excellence in Mining (iCEM) is 
driving innovation through applied technology 
development, emerging mining solutions and the 
advancement of critical mineral technologies. The Gujarat 
Mineral Research Industrial Consultancy Society (GMRICS) 
is strengthening exploration through geological 
investigations, resource evaluation and mineral 
intelligence . The GMDC Science & Research Centre (GSRC) 
is advancing research through scientiﬁc studies, mineral 
analysis, technical development and capacity building 
across the mining ecosystem. Together with initiatives such 
the GMDC Young Leaders Programme , these institutions 
are nurturing the next generation of leaders, researchers 
and mining professionals who will shape GMDC' s long-term 
growth and strategic ambitions.Continuing Our Commitment to Shared Prosperity
While minerals deﬁne our business, people deﬁne our 
purpose . This belief continues to shape GMDC’ s approach 
to community development through Gramya Vikas Trust 
(GVT), whose work across Gujarat and Odisha focusses on 
creating opportunities that endure well beyond our 
operational footprint. During the year, our education and 
scholarship initiatives supported more than 26,000 
students, while mobile healthcare services reached 
over 40,000 people. Through Samarthya, more than 
6,500 youth and women were supported through 
vocational training, entrepreneurship and livelihood 
generation. Alongside these eﬀorts, water management, 
sanitation, community infrastructure and other social 
interventions are helping create an ecosystem where 
communities can grow with greater access and better 
opportunity .
Excellence through People & Practices
During the year under review , GMDC’ s work received 
recognition across responsible mining, sustainable mineral 
development and community impact. Among the notable 
honours were the National Geoscience Award for 
Sustainable Mineral Development and the Golden Peacock 
Award for Corporate Social Responsibility 2025, conferred 
by the Institute of Directors, New Delhi. GMDC-GVT’ s 
sustained and systematic approach to community 
development has also been recognised through the FIMI 
Sitaram Rungta Award. 
Alongside these achievements, GMDC is strengthening its 
people practices through Rising HR, a transformation 
initiative designed to build a more employee-centric and 
future-ready organisation. Built around ﬁve pillars of 
Digitisation & Automation, Talent & Capability Building, 
Employee Experience & Culture, Data-Driven HR and 
Compliance & Governance , Rising HR will strengthen how 
GMDC develops talent, supports employees and prepares 
its workforce for the Company’ s next phase of growth.
As custodians of strategic natural resources, we recognise 
that our responsibility extends far beyond mining. It is to 
strengthen India's resource security, create resilient 
domestic value chains, encourage innovation and ensure 
that the nation 's natural wealth continues to generate 
sustainable value for generations to come .
I extend my sincere appreciation to our employees for their 
dedication, to our Board for its guidance, to the 
Government of Gujarat and the Government of India for 
their continued support, and to our shareholders, partners, 
customers and the communities around our operations for 
the trust they continue to place in GMDC. Their conﬁdence 
inspires us to continue raising our aspirations and 
delivering with integrity .
Warm regards,
Roopwant Singh, IA S
Managing Director, GMDC

A Year of Expanding and Growing 
CRITICAL MINERALS

=== page 15 ===
India 's growth story is entering a deﬁning phase . As the 
country advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 
@2047 , it is simultaneously expanding its manufacturing 
base, modernising infrastructure, accelerating 
digitalisation and improving the quality of life for over 1.4 
billion people . Every one of these ambitions is underpinned 
by one critical enabler – energy .
India 's energy demand is driven by more than its population 
growth, it is driven by Industrial expansion, urbanisation, 
electriﬁcation, rapid adoption of cooling technologies, data 
centres, electric mobility and new-age manufacturing are 
reshaping the country' s energy proﬁle . Together , they are 
creating one of the fastest-growing electricity markets in 
the world.
India is expected to remain among the world' s fastest-
growing electricity markets through the end of the decade . 
According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), 
electricity demand is projected to grow at an average 
6.4% annually through 2030 , adding more than 570 TWh of 
new annual electricity consumption over the next ﬁve years 
– equivalent to creating the electricity demand of several 
industrialised nations.A New Era of Energy Security
As demand rises, energy security is becoming increasingly 
strategic. India 's focus is now on ensuring that energy 
remains reliable , aﬀordable , resilient and increasingly self-
reliant. Recent geopolitical disruptions and supply-chain 
uncertainties have reinforced the importance of 
strengthening domestic energy resources while 
maintaining a balanced energy mix capable of supporting 
continuous economic growth. The country's energy 
transition is therefore not a replacement of conventional 
energy with renewables. It is the creation of an integrated 
energy ecosystem where renewable energy , conventional 
fuels, storage technologies and transmission infrastructure 
work together to deliver dependable power .
The Strategic Role of Indigenous Resources. 
It is within this larger national imperative that 
GMDC is contributing to India 's energy security 
by developing the domestic resources that 
sustain economic growth, strengthen industrial 
competitiveness and support reliable power 
generation. While India accelerates its transition 
towards cleaner sources of energy , the nation 's 
immediate energy requirements continue to 
depend on a resilient and balanced energy 
ecosystem. GMDC remains committed to 
responsibly developing the resources that 
support this transition while reinforcing India 's 
long-term energy resilience . India's

As India advances towards a cleaner energy future, 
ensuring reliable and aﬀordable energy remains just as 
important as expanding renewable capacity . For a rapidly 
growing economy, energy security depends on 
maintaining a balanced energy mix where conventional 
and renewable resources complement one another . In this 
landscape , lignite continues to play a vital role by providing 
dependable baseload power , supporting energy-intensive 
industries and reducing dependence on imported fuels.
For Gujarat, lignite has been far more than a mineral 
resource . It has fuelled industries, strengthened regional 
economies and laid the foundation for one of India 's most 
vibrant manufacturing ecosystems. At the centre of this 
journey has been GMDC, which has built one of India ’s 
largest lignite resource portfolios over more than ﬁve 
decades.A Steadily Strengthening Resource
GMDC’ s lignite journey began with the Panandhro Lignite 
Mine , commissioned in 1973, marking the beginning of 
commercial lignite mining in Gujarat. The mine went on to 
become a major source of domestic fuel for the State’s 
emerging industrial economy .
Following Panandhro , GMDC progressively expanded its 
lignite footprint across Gujarat. The Rajpardi Lignite Mine , 
commissioned in 1984, extended GMDC’ s presence into 
South Gujarat, followed by Mata no Madh in 2002, 
Tadkeshwar in 2005 and Bhavnagar in 2008. Umarsar , 
commissioned in 2015, further strengthened GMDC’s 
lignite base in Kutch. Most recently , Lakhpat Punhrajpur 
was commissioned in 2026, marking the next step in this 
steadily expanding journey .
Today , GMDC is India ’s No. 1 Merchant Seller of Lignite , with 
its mining portfolio continuing to evolve to meet the State’s 
changing energy and industrial requirements.

coal mines hold more than 2 billion tonnes of geological

contributors towards immediate energy security .

At the heart of this transformation, Baitarani West is the 
ﬂagship project of GMDC' s commercial coal portfolio . With

tonnes of mineable reserves and a planned peak 
production capacity of 15 MTP A, Baitarani W est is not only 
poised to become GMDC' s largest mining asset, but also 
one of India 's Top 20 coal-producing mines by annual 
production capacity . The project has moved decisively 
from planning to execution. During the year under review , 
GMDC achieved signiﬁcant progress through statutory 
approvals, land acquisition and rehabilitation planning, 
while also obtaining key environmental and forest 
clearances and appointing its Agency for Mine

Bauxite is often viewed through the lens of aluminium. In 
practice , its industrial relevance is broader . In Gujarat, 
bauxite from Kutch and Devbhoomi Dwarka supports a 
range of downstream industries including chemicals, 
refractory, cement, aluminium and abrasive industries. 
GMDC is mining bauxite through its Gadhsisa group of 
mines and Mevasa, with the current oﬃcial site listing the 
Gadhsisa mines at Daban-Wamoti, Mothala-Balachod, 
Nana-Goniyasar , Naredi Nandra, Naredi-I & II, Ratadia-
Nagrecha, Roha-Kotada and Wandh-I & II, alongside 
Mevasa.
A Portfolio Built for Diverse Industries
With operations at Mevasa  and the Gadhsisa Group of 
Mines in Devbhoomi Dwaka and Kutch respectively,  
GMDC has developed one of Gujarat' s largest bauxite 
portfolios, backed by nearly 27.5 million tonnes of 
resources spread across 11 mining leases. Unlike 
conventional bauxite operations focussed on a single end-
use, GMDC' s portfolio caters to multiple industries through 
high grade, medium grade and low grade materials, 
enabling supply across cement, refractories, chemicals, 
ceramics and abrasive manufacturing. This diversiﬁed 
market base enhances commercial ﬂexibility while 
reducing dependence on any one sector .Changing the Economics of Bauxite
The transformation of GMDC' s bauxite business has been 
driven not by discovering new resources, but by extracting 
greater value from existing ones.
The Company successfully monetised over 0.2 MT of 
legacy inventory through transparent, market-driven 
auctions, demonstrating that medium and low-grade 
bauxite can generate strong commercial returns when 
matched with the right industries. Rather than treating 
inventory as dormant stock, GMDC repositioned it as a 
strategic asset, creating new opportunities for customers 
while improving capital eﬃciency .
At the same time, a focussed programme of customer 
outreach, technical discussions, roadshows and industry 
engagement expanded the customer base by 33%, 
strengthening relationships with cement manufacturers, 
refractory producers and ceramic industries. This market-
led approach transformed GMDC from a supplier of raw 
material into a responsive mineral partner capable of 
delivering application-speciﬁc solutions.Bauxite

As the world's second-largest cement producer, India 
continues to witness unprecedented demand for cement, 
driven by rapid urbanisation, expanding industrial capacity 
and transformative national programmes such as PM Gati 
Shakti, Bharatmala, Sagarmala and the country' s growing 
housing and infrastructure ambitions. At the heart of this 
growth lies limestone-the single-most important raw 
material for cement manufacturing and one of the country' s 
most strategic infrastructure minerals. With abundant high-
grade limestone resources and world-class logistics 
connectivity , Gujarat is uniquely positioned to support this 
next phase of nation-building. Within Gujarat, Western 
Kutch stands out as one of India 's most promising limestone 
provinces, oﬀering the scale and quality required to create 
a globally competitive cement manufacturing ecosystem.
GMDC' s limestone strategy is centred on partnerships that 
convert mineral wealth into long-term economic 
development. Under Limestone Wave I, the Company 
successfully oﬀered nearly 800 million tonnes of limestone 
reserves through a transparent competitive bidding 
process, culminating in a 40-year Limestone Supply 
Agreement with JK Cement Ltd. and City Gold Pipes Pvt. 
Ltd. (a consortium of Goldcrest Cement Pvt. Ltd. and Kailash 
Darshan Housing Development, Gujarat), for establishing a 
greenﬁeld integrated cement plant in Western Kutch.
Building on this momentum, Limestone Wave II is being 
advanced around the Panandhro Extension deposits, while 
Wave III will unlock the signiﬁcant limestone resources at 
Bharkandam, ensuring a long-term pipeline for industrial 
expansion and resource optimisation.Adding further momentum, the GMDC Board has approved 
the opening of the Lakhpat Punhrajpur Integrated Lignite 
and Limestone Project, which is now operation-ready , with 
a peak rated capacity of 29.81 MTPA. This addition is set to 
signiﬁcantly strengthening the Company' s ability to support 
Gujarat' s growing cement industry while reinforcing long-
term resource security .
Building Regional Prosperity
The true value of limestone extends well beyond cement. 
Every new cement plant catalyses an ecosystem of 
economic activity–creating employment, attracting 
ancillary industries, strengthening logistics infrastructure 
and generating long-term revenue through royalties, taxes 
and District Mineral Foundation contributions. By 
responsibly developing its limestone resources, GMDC is 
not merely supplying a mineral; it is enabling industrial 
clusters that create enduring value for communities, 
businesses and the nation.
As India accelerates towards becoming a developed 
economy , GMDC' s limestone portfolio will continue to 
provide one of the most fundamental building blocks of 
future-ready infrastructure .Limestone

Enabling the Energy Transition
Creating pathways towards a cleaner and more resilient future
India 's energy transition requires more than a shift from 
conventional resources. It calls for stronger domestic 
resource security , lower import dependence and new 
technologies that can convert India 's own resources into 
cleaner energy alongside adding value to industrial and 
consumer sectors. GMDC is building this transition across 
two pathways: expanding its renewable energy portfolio 
while advancing Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation as a new 
route for unlocking domestic lignite and coal resources.
Renewable energy is an established part of GMDC's 
diversiﬁed energy portfolio. During FY 2025-26, the 
Company's 205.9 MW renewable portfolio generated 
333.5 million units of electricity and ₹130.4 crore in 
revenue . The portfolio comprises seven wind projects with 
a combined capacity of 200.9 MW and the 5 MW 
Panandhro Solar Project.
Wind remained the principal contributor , generating 327.1 
MU during the year compared with 320 .9 MU in FY 2024-
25. The portfolio generated ₹127.3 crore in revenue. Rojmal, with 50 MW of installed capacity , remained the 
largest generator at 84.6 MU while Varvala  recorded the 
strongest year-on-year growth with generation increasing 
by 30%  to 36.4 MU. Bhanvad generated 81.0 MU while 
Jodiya contributed 53.7 MU.
The 5 MW Panandhro Solar Project generated 6.4 MU 
during the year and contributed ₹3.1 crore  in revenue . 
Together , the wind and solar assets generated 333.5 MU 
compared with 327.5 MU in FY 2024-25.
The Company has also initiated a strategic intervention in 
solar and hybrid C&I power generation,  with a dedicated 
internal committee working on location identiﬁcation, SPV 
structures and engagement with industrial power 
consumers for long-term partnerships. Plans to repurpose 
mined-out land for clean energy installations create an 
additional link between land restoration and renewable 
energy development.Renewable Energy

=== page 28 ===
For nearly two decades, the power station at Akrimota has 
stood as a distinctive part of GMDC’ s journey from mineral 
development to integrated energy . Commissioned as a 
2 × 125 MW lignite-based power station, it represented a 
natural extension of the Company’s core strength: 
transforming indigenous mineral resources into 
dependable energy . Today , that journey enters a new 
chapter. Following a comprehensive revival and 
turnaround programme , Akrimota Thermal Power Station 
has been repositioned as Lakhpat Thermal Power Station 
(LTPS).  Located in Lakhpat Tehsil of Kutch and linked to 
GMDC’ s Lakhpat Punhrajpur and Panandhro Extension 
Lignite Mines, LTPS represents the renewal of a strategic 
energy asset and a stronger integration of the Company’ s 
lignite and power businesses.
The journey towards LTPS began with the Board’ s approval 
in February 2023 for the revival of ATPS and the 
associated turnaround programme. The initiative was 
undertaken to restore the operating capability of the plant, 
strengthen reliability and bring its generating units back 
into service .
A Turnaround Completed
The turnaround was structured into six packages, 
executed by ﬁve reputed contractors, with L&T Sargent & 
Lundy Ltd. providing Project Management Consultancy 
services and overseeing on-site execution.
A key milestone was achieved with the successful 
turnaround and synchronisation of both units. Unit 2 was 
synchronised on 5 September 2025,  following boiler light-
up on 22 August 2025. Unit 1 was synchronised on 9 
January 2026,  following boiler light-up on 1 January 2026. 
Unit 1 is currently under stabilisation, with generation 
continuing to improve .
The successful synchronisation of both units marks the 
restoration of the station as an operational part of GMDC’ s 
integrated lignite-to-power value chain.A Name Aligned with its Future
The transition from ATPS to Lakhpat Thermal Power 
Station reﬂects more than a change in nomenclature . The 
new name corresponds to the station ’s physical location in 
Lakhpat Tehsil  and its long-term association with the 
Lakhpat Punhrajpur and Panandhro Extension Lignite 
Mines.
The renaming also establishes a common identity for future 
project documentation, statutory correspondence, 
contractual documents and stakeholder communications 
and aligns the station with GMDC’ s future operational and 
business strategy .
Strengthening the Lignite-to-P ower Value Chain
LTPS connects GMDC’s lignite resources with power 
generation through a locally anchored fuel-to-power 
model. Its linkage with GMDC’ s emerging lignite mines 
creates a stronger foundation for the long-term utilisation 
of these resources while reinforcing the strategic role of 
power generation within GMDC’ s diversiﬁed portfolio .
With both units synchronised and performance continuing 
to stabilise, LTPS is positioned for its next phase of 
operation with a focus on reliability , optimisation and 
sustained generation.
Completing the Turnaround
With the core turnaround activities completed, the 
ﬁnalisation and closure of contracts across the various 
packages is underway. The ﬁnal contract values will 
subsequently be placed before the Board.
GMDC is also preparing a petition for submission to the 
Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) 
seeking approval for the additional capital expenditure 
incurred during the turnaround.Renewing a Strategic Energy AssetLakhpat Thermal Power Station (LTPS)rd

Pr140.908Entering a New Resource Age
As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @2047 , resource 
security is emerging as a strategic national priority . From 
clean energy and advanced manufacturing to defence and 
high technology , access to critical minerals will increasingly 
shape the country’s industrial competitiveness and 
economic resilience .
A new resource economy is taking shape alongside this 
transition. The mineral requirements of an industrialising 
and increasingly technology-intensive world are evolving 
as electriﬁcation, digital infrastructure, advanced 
manufacturing, aerospace, defence and emerging 
technologies increase demand for materials with 
specialised physical, chemical and magnetic properties. In 
this environment, the strategic importance of a mineral is 
increasingly determined not merely by its geological 
availability , but by its relevance to essential technologies 
and the resilience of the supply chains through which it 
reaches industry .
This has also brought greater attention to the geographical 
concentration of critical mineral supply chains. For 
economies seeking to build competitive manufacturing 
sectors, secure access to minerals must increasingly be 
complemented by domestic capabilities in beneﬁciation, 
processing, separation, materials development and 
recycling. The ability to convert a mineral resource into 
industrially usable material is therefore becoming as 
important as access to the resource itself .Recognising this shift, the Government of India has 
launched the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) to 
strengthen the entire value chain – from exploration and 
mining to beneﬁciation, processing and recycling – while 
reducing dependence on imports and building a self-reliant 
mineral ecosystem.
The Mission reﬂects a wider strategic imperative for India: 
to build resilience across mineral supply chains that 
support the country’ s economic expansion, technological 
capabilities and advanced manufacturing ambitions. 
Developing domestic mineral-processing capabilities can 
also enable greater value addition within the country and 
create stronger linkages between India’s geological 
resources and its growing industrial base .
Aligned with this national vision, GMDC is expanding its 
capabilities in strategic minerals, laying the foundation for a 
future-ready resource portfolio that supports India ’s long-
term industrial and technological ambitions. In doing so, the 
Company is progressively broadening the conventional 
role of a mineral resource developer – from extraction

Metals that Will Power India 's Next Chapter
Copper , lead and zinc are integral to a wide range of 
industries shaping India 's future . Copper is essential for 
renewable energy systems, electric mobility, power 
transmission, electronics and defence manufacturing. Zinc 
protects steel infrastructure from corrosion, extending the 
life of bridges, railways and industrial assets, while lead 
continues to serve important applications in automotive 
and backup energy storage batteries. By developing these 
resources within India, Ambaji can strengthen the domestic 
availability of metals that underpin the country's 
infrastructure , manufacturing and energy systems.
From Ore to Concentrates
The proposed mine will use underground mining methods, 
with ore accessed through underground declines and 
extracted through mechanised stoping supported by 
cemented rock ﬁll. The extracted ore will then undergo 
crushing, grinding, ﬂotation and ﬁltration to produce 
separate copper, lead and zinc concentrates. By 
integrating mining with beneﬁciation, the project is 
designed to create greater value from the polymetallic 
resource while establishing domestic processing 
capability .
Strengthening India 's Mineral Self-R eliance
The development of Ambaji is aligned with India 's broader 
pursuit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and mineral self-reliance . A 
domestic source of copper , lead and zinc concentrates can 
strengthen supply-chain resilience and support industries 
that currently depend on secure access to these essential 
raw materials.
The project also assumes greater signiﬁcance as India 's 
requirements for copper grow with the expansion of 
renewable power, electric mobility, transmission 
infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. In this context, 
Ambaji connects Gujarat' s mineral resources with India 's 
long-term industrial and energy ambitions.Creating Value Beyond the Mine
The project is expected to generate direct and indirect 
employment while creating economic activity across 
mining, mineral processing, engineering, logistics and 
ancillary services. Its development can also strengthen the 
surrounding regional economy by creating opportunities

planned operating life, Ambaji is positioned to create 
lasting value for Gujarat while contributing to India's 
domestic base-metal supply .
Advancing Towards Development

development milestones. The Mining Plan was approved 
by the Indian Bureau of Mines in July 2025, followed by

GEMI.
Exploration continues to strengthen the resource base .

Underground Coal Gasication 
Unlocking New Energy & Resource Value Chain
India 's energy challenge is not only about how much coal is 
available . It is also about how much of that resource can be 
accessed through conventional mining. Around 43% of 
India's coal resources lie too deep for conventional 
mining, even as the country imports approximately 
USD 21 billion worth of coal every year. Underground Coal 
Gasiﬁcation presents a diﬀerent proposition: converting 
deep-seated coal or lignite into a usable energy and 
industrial feedstock without conventional mining.
This distinction is important. Conventional coal 
development is centred on bringing a solid resource to the 
surface , after which it is transported and used principally as 
an energy source or industrial fuel. UCG changes this 
sequence by taking the conversion process underground. 
The coal remains in place and, under controlled conditions, 
is converted within the seam into synthesis gas, or Syngas, 
which can subsequently be recovered at the surface .
In doing so, UCG creates a possible route for evaluating 
selected deeper, diﬃcult-to-access or potentially 
uneconomic coal and lignite resources that may not lend 
themselves readily to conventional mining. It can therefore 
expand the strategic conversation around coal – from how 
much can be mined to how eﬀectively the resource can be 
converted and integrated into higher-value industrial 
chains.
The Government of India has identiﬁed Coal Gasiﬁcation 
as a strategic national priority under the country' s Viksit 
Bharat @2047 vision. The objective is to maximise the 
value of domestic coal resources, strengthen energy 
security, reduce import dependence and create new 
industrial value chains. With one of India 's largest lignite reserves and an established industrial ecosystem, Gujarat 
is well positioned to evaluate this technology. The 
Government of Gujarat has entrusted GMDC to lead the 
State's UCG initiatives.
For GMDC, this represents an evolution in how domestic 
resources can create value . Instead of limiting lignite to its 
conventional use as a fuel, UCG creates a pathway to 
convert underground lignite into Syngas, opening 
applications across energy , chemicals, fuels and advanced 
manufacturing. This establishes the foundation for a wider 
resource-conversion model,  in which the value of the 
resource is derived not only from the coal or lignite itself , 
but from the portfolio of products that can potentially be 
manufactured from the resulting Syngas.
The proposition is strategic, but it is equally dependent on 
disciplined technical development. UCG cannot be treated 
as universally applicable across coal resources. Geological 
conﬁguration, seam depth and thickness, permeability , 
faults and fractures, groundwater systems, coal properties 
and surface conditions can materially inﬂuence project 
suitability . Establishing the technology therefore requires 
detailed investigation, modelling, pilot-scale  
demonstration and continuous environmental oversight.
The longer-term opportunity lies in combining India's 
domestic resource base with technology-led conversion 
and downstream manufacturing capabilities. If technically , 
environmentally and commercially validated, UCG can 
provide an additional pathway for creating value from 
selected indigenous coal and lignite resources while 
supporting a broader industrial ecosystem around Syngas.rd

36From Coal Seam to Syngas
Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation is an in-situ gasiﬁcation 
process. Coal or lignite remains underground while the 
conversion takes place within the seam. The process 
begins with injection and production wells drilled from the 
surface to the target coal seam. Air or oxygen, along with 
steam where required, is then introduced into the seam. A 
controlled underground reaction converts the coal into 
Syngas. The gas is brought to the surface through the 
production well and subsequently processed into industrial 
products.
The operating sequence is captured in the ﬁve-step 
framework presented in UCG concept – Drill, Inject, 
Gasify , Produce and Utilise.  Injection and production wells 
provide controlled access to the target seam. The injection 
system supplies the oxidant required to initiate and sustain 
the reaction, while the production system provides the 
pathway through which the resulting gases are recovered.
Within the coal seam, part of the coal is oxidised to 
generate the heat required to support subsequent 
gasiﬁcation reactions. The underground reaction zone is 
then progressively controlled so that the surrounding coal 
is converted into gaseous products. Unlike conventional 
mining, where value is created by physically removing the 
coal, UCG seeks to recover the energy and chemical 
potential of the resource in gaseous form.
The resulting Syngas typically contains a combination of 
hydrogen, carbon mono xide, methane, carbon dioxide 
and other constituents, although its exact composition 
varies according to the coal or lignite characteristics, 
oxidant used, operating conditions and underground 
reaction behaviour. This variability matters because 
diﬀerent downstream processes require diﬀerent gas 
speciﬁcations.Syngas intended for power generation, for example , can 
have diﬀerent conditioning requirements from Syngas that 
is to become a feedstock for methanol, ammonia or 
synthetic fuels. Consequently, the gas produced 
underground generally requires appropriate surface 
treatment. Depending upon its composition and intended 
use, this may include removal of particulates, moisture , 
sulphur compounds and other impurities, followed by gas 
conditioning and adjustment of the required process-gas 
composition.
Surface facilities therefore form an important part of the 
overall UCG system. The underground conversion process 
produces the raw Syngas; the surface processing system 
turns that gas into a ﬁt-for-purpose feedstock. Together , 
these elements create a continuous chain from the coal 
seam to an energy product, chemical intermediate or 
industrial feedstock.
One of UCG' s principal strategic attractions is its potential 
application to coal or lignite resources that may be diﬃcult 
to exploit conventionally because of depth, mining 
complexity or economics. Conversion in situ can potentially 
reduce the need to physically extract and transport large 
quantities of solid coal. This does not, however , remove the 
environmental or technical responsibilities associated with 
developing the resource; rather , it changes their nature .
Subsurface understanding becomes particularly important. 
The target seam and the rocks above , below and around it 
need to be characterised in suﬃcient detail to understand 
gas movement, water movement and the behaviour of the 
underground reaction. Geological faults, fractures and 
connections with aquifers can inﬂuence the design and 
feasibility of a project.Injection and

=== page 38 ===
Groundwater protection is therefore central to responsible 
UCG development. Baseline hydrogeological information, 
monitoring networks, control of operating conditions and 
continued observation during and after a pilot can help 
establish whether the reaction zone remains appropriately 
contained. Surface emissions, produced water where 
applicable, gas quality and changes in subsurface 
conditions similarly require systematic monitoring.
UCG should consequently be viewed as an integrated 
technology comprising resource characterisation, 
subsurface conversion, well engineering, gas processing, 
environmental safeguards and continuous monitoring. 
Pilot-scale validation provides the critical setting in which 
these diﬀerent components can be tested together before 
consideration of larger-scale deployment.
One Resource, Multiple Value Chains
The signiﬁcance of UCG extends beyond the production of 
gas. Syngas becomes the building block for an extensive 
downstream industrial ecosystem, creating opportunities 
to convert a domestic resource into higher-value products. 
GMDC' s UCG platform has the potential to support 13+ 
sectors through downstream applications spanning fuels, 
chemicals, fertilisers, industrial materials and power .
The existing UCG framework identiﬁes a wide range of 
potential applications. Under fuels, these include 
methanol, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, Fischer-T ropsch 
fuels, ethanol and synthetic natural gas. Chemical 
pathways include acetic acid, mono ethylene glycol and 
formaldehyde, while fertiliser and industrial product 
pathways include ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate and 
ammonium sulphate. The platform can also potentially 
support Direct Reduced Iron and at-pit power generation.
This range illustrates why Syngas is strategically diﬀerent 
from a conventional fuel. Syngas is an intermediate 
platform. Through appropriate puriﬁcation, separation and 
synthesis, the carbon mono xide and hydrogen contained in 
the gas can potentially be converted into several diﬀerent 
products. Hydrogen can itself become an industrial 
feedstock or serve as an intermediate in the manufacture of 
ammonia, methanol and other products.For power applications, conditioned Syngas can potentially 
be utilised close to the resource location, creating the 
possibility of at-pit or mine-mouth conversion. For 
chemicals and fuels, it can enter synthesis processes that 
progressively transform the gaseous feedstock into higher-
value molecules. For metallurgical applications such as 
Direct Reduced Iron, suitable gas streams may provide 
another potential industrial pathway .
The signiﬁcance for GMDC is that the same underground 
resource need not necessarily be associated with a single 
product. Depending upon project conﬁguration and market 
requirements, UCG could support an anchor downstream 
application supplemented over time by other product 
chains.  The optimal route would emerge from technical 
and commercial assessment rather than from attempting to 
develop every possible pathway simultaneously .
Syngas composition will be a key determinant. The 
hydrogen-to-carbon mono xide relationship , concentration 
of methane and carbon dioxide, presence of impurities and 
overall caloriﬁc value inﬂuence which applications are 
technically suitable and what level of gas cleaning or 
conditioning is required. Pilot operations can therefore 
provide information not only about gasiﬁcation 
performance , but also about the downstream industries 
that a particular resource may realistically support.
Economics are equally important. Product selection would 
need to consider plant scale , processing requirements, 
infrastructure , access to water and power , transportation 
costs, proximity to markets and competitive feedstock 
alternatives. Market demand and the presence of existing 
downstream industrial clusters can further shape the 
eventual conﬁguration.rd

ﬁnal value realised. This is the essence of One Resource , 
Multiple Value Chains – not the simultaneous development 
of every pathway , but the ability to select and build the 
pathways that create the greatest strategic and economic

stated focus includes carbon footprint reduction, energy 
conservation and technologies such as coal and lignite 
gasiﬁcation and Blue Hydrogen.
=== page 41 ===
Preparing Mining for a Lower Carbon Future
The path to net zero will require a combination of 
technologies rather than a single solution. GMDC is  
therefore building capabilities across the technology chain, 
evaluating solutions that can reduce emissions from mining 
operations while creating cleaner pathways for the 
utilisation of domestic resources. In areas such as 
Underground Coal Gasiﬁcation and cleaner mining 
mobility , iCEM supported the initial stages by facilitating 
preliminary studies, technology assessments and pre-
feasibility work. This early-stage eﬀort helped GMDC 
assess potential opportunities, understand their technical 
and commercial context and develop an initial pathway for 
further action. Following these preliminary assessments, 
GMDC has taken forward the initiatives and is driving their 
subsequent evaluation and development, with iCEM 
continuing to provide research, knowledge and technical 
support where relevant.
For gasiﬁcation, iCEM helped initiate and facilitate the 
preliminary assessment of opportunities for GMDC. 
Building on this groundwork, GMDC is now taking forward 
the development of its gasiﬁcation initiatives as part of its 
wider eﬀort to unlock greater value from domestic 
resources and assess cleaner industrial pathways.
A similar progression is taking place in mine transportation. 
iCEM initiated the early assessment of Zero Emission 
Trucking for GMDC and supported the preparation of the 
preliminary/PFR-level feasibility assessment. This work 
provided an initial basis for evaluating the potential 
application of zero-emission haulage technologies in 
mining conditions. GMDC has subsequently taken 
ownership of evaluating and progressing cleaner mine-
haulage solutions.
As part of this eﬀort, GMDC is also exploring the induction 
of LNG trucks in its mining operations. LNG-based trucking 
represents a cleaner , lower-emission transitional option 
compared with conventional mine-haulage fuels, while 
longer-term evaluation continues around zero-emission 
mobility solutions. Together , these pathways allow GMDC 
to consider near-term opportunities for reducing the 
environmental intensity of mine transportation while 
continuing to assess technologies that could enable 
deeper emissions reductions over time. These initiatives 
complement ongoing work on energy conservation, 
renewable energy integration, water conservation and 
digital technologies, creating a broader framework for 
reducing the environmental intensity of mining.
The focus is on moving promising technologies 
progressively from concept and preliminary assessment 
towards informed decision-making and, where 
appropriate, further development. Early-stage techno-
commercial studies, technology evaluations and pre-
feasibility assessments supported by iCEM help build the 
knowledge base required for this process, while GMDC 
determines the subsequent development andimplementation pathway. This approach is particularly 
relevant as India seeks to decarbonise sectors where 
alternatives to conventional fuels and processes remain 
diﬃcult to deploy .
iCEM continues to support this broader eﬀort through 
research, knowledge development, technology 
assessment and technical inputs that can inform GMDC' s 
strategic and investment decision-making.
Carbon Management Pathways
Carbon management is emerging as an important part of 
India 's decarbonisation pathway , particularly for hard to 
abate sectors. NITI Aayog has identiﬁed CCUS (Carbon 
Capture , Utilisation, and Storage) as a potential strategy for 
deep decarbonisation while the Government' s 2025 CCUS 
R&D roadmap is intended to accelerate technology 
development and deployment across sectors such as 
power , cement and steel.
For GMDC, carbon management is being explored as part 
of a wider technology pathway rather than as a standalone 
intervention. The Company is evaluating Carbon Capture , 
Utilisation and Storage alongside gasiﬁcation and Blue 
Hydrogen, drawing on research, knowledge and technical 
inputs from iCEM where relevant. The underlying 
opportunity is to capture carbon from suitable industrial 
processes and either utilise it as a feedstock or manage it 
through appropriate storage pathways, thereby reducing 
the carbon intensity of industrial activity .
GMDC' s approach is focussed on building knowledge and 
technology capability before scaling deployment. By 
evaluating emerging technologies, strengthening 
renewable generation, improving energy eﬃciency and 
exploring carbon-management pathways, the Company is 
preparing its operations and future businesses for an 
economy where resource productivity and carbon 
performance will increasingly go hand-in-hand.

Digitilisation: Mining with a Digital Edge
Mining has always depended on geology , engineering and 
operational excellence . Today , it is increasingly driven by 
something equally valuable – intelligence . Every drill, haul 
truck, weighbridge and despatch generates data that can 
improve productivity, strengthen safety and optimise 
resources. The ability to convert this information into timely 
decisions is reshaping the future of mining. GMDC is 
building this capability through an integrated digital 
ecosystem that connects operations, logistics and 
business processes. By embedding AI, IoT, automation and 
advanced analytics across its value chain, the Company is 
creating a mining enterprise that is more connected, more 
responsive and better equipped to support its expanding 
scale of operations.
Building a Connected & Secure Enterprise
As GMDC grows beyond lignite into a diversiﬁed natural 
resources company , its digital infrastructure is evolving 
alongside it. During the year, the Company strengthened its 
enterprise technology landscape through cloud-based 
platforms, integrated business systems and enhanced 
cybersecurity . Oracle ERP was migrated to Oracle Cloud 
Infrastructure while Microsoft 365 strengthened 
collaboration and communication across the organisation. 
Together , these initiatives are creating a secure , scalable 
and agile digital backbone capable of supporting faster 
execution and better governance .

Leading Future-ready Breakthroughs
Catalysing India 's Critical Minerals and Net Zero 
Transition
Mining is entering a deﬁning decade . As nations race to 
secure critical minerals, decarbonise industries and build 
resilient supply chains, innovation is becoming as 
important as the resources themselves. The ability to 
develop new technologies, validate emerging solutions 
and build specialised capabilities will determine how 
successfully countries navigate the transition towards a low 
carbon future .
Established under the aegis of GMDC and supported by the 
Government of Gujarat, the International Centre of 
Excellence in Mining (iCEM) is building that bridge. 
Conceived as a centre for research, innovation and 
collaboration, iCEM is creating the technologies, 
knowledge and capabilities that will shape the future of 
mining in India. By bringing together minerals, technology 
and people under the shared imperative of sustainability , 
the Centre is helping build an ecosystem that supports 
resource security , energy independence and the transition 
towards a low carbon future .

Where Ideas Become Industry
At iCEM, promising technologies are evaluated through 
techno-commercial pre-feasibility studies, laboratory and 
bench scale testing, advanced analytical facilities and pilot 
scale validation before they are considered for wider 
deployment. This integrated approach enables the Centre 
to assess technical feasibility , commercial viability and 
operational-readiness, helping accelerate the adoption of 
breakthrough solutions across the mining sector . Its work 
spans transformative technologies including Underground 
Coal Gasiﬁcation, Carbon Capture , Blue Hydrogen, Zero 
Emission Transport and intelligent mining systems, creating 
practical pathways towards cleaner , more eﬃcient and 
future-ready mining operations.
Building Intelligence for Critical Minerals
Critical minerals are rapidly becoming strategic assets for 
economic growth, clean energy and technological 
leadership . Recognising this shift, iCEM is leading the 
development of the Critical Minerals Supply Chain 
Observatory in partnership with the University of 
Cambridge under the India–UK Technology Security 
Initiative (TSI). The Observatory a cloud native , AI-enabled 
platform, is designed to map end-to-end supply chains for 
minerals, with a special focus on rare earth elements, for 
providing geographically-veriﬁed intelligence, supply 
chain stress testing, environmental assessment, regulatory transparency and digital ESG auditing. This Observatory 
will strengthen decision-making across government and 
industry while reinforcing Gujarat' s leadership in building 
resilient and sustainable mineral ecosystems.
Creating Capability for the Next Generation
Alongside research and innovation, iCEM is investing in the 
human capabilities that will deﬁne the future of mining. 
Through specialised training programmes, leadership 
development initiatives and collaborative research, the 
Centre is nurturing professionals equipped to lead 
sustainable mining, emerging technologies and digital 
transformation. Its partnerships with government agencies, 
industry leaders, academic institutions and global research 
organisations ensure that knowledge is shared, innovation 
is accelerated and emerging technologies move more 
rapidly from concept to commercial application.
Shaping the Future of Mining
The  mining  sector  is  entering  an  era  where 
competitiveness will depend on the ability to innovate , 
collaborate and adapt. By connecting scientiﬁc research 
with industrial application, developing future technologies, 
strengthening critical mineral capabilities and building the 
talent required for tomorrow , iCEM is helping deﬁne this 
new era.

Mapping Gujarat's Resource Future
Reading Resource-R eadiness, Layer by Layer
From the lignite ﬁelds of Kutch and South Gujarat to the 
copper-bearing formations of Ambaji, the ﬂuorite and 
associated metal-bearing carbonatites of Ambadungar , the 
limestone belts of western Kutch and the bauxite deposits 
of Gadhsisa and Mevasa, GMRICS is expanding the 
geological understanding of Gujarat through integrated 
exploration. GMRICS's holistic exploration programme 
combines geological mapping, geophysical investigations, 
exploratory drilling, mineralogical and geochemical 
analysis and three-dimensional resource modelling to 
improve the accuracy of resource estimation and support 
future mine planning. This scientiﬁc approach enables 
GMDC to make informed investment decisions while 
accelerating the responsible development of mineral 
resources.
Expanding the Copper Story at Ambaji
One of GMRICS' s most signiﬁcant programmes is the 
ongoing exploration of the Ambaji Copper Belt, supporting 
GMDC's vision of establishing one of western India's 
important integrated copper projects. The current 
exploration programme targets one lakh metres of drilling 
over three years, with 25,000 metres undertaken during 
the year across both brownﬁeld and greenﬁeld prospects. 
To facilitate exploration, an on-site laboratory has been 
established, equipped with state-of-the-art comminution 
and petrographic equipment. Integrated exploration 
combining geological mapping, drilling, geophysical 
logging and chemical analysis has helped conﬁrm the ore 
body conﬁguration and identify encouraging copper and 
zinc-lead mineralisation, strengthening conﬁdence in the 
deposit' s long-term development potential.Unlocking Greater Value from Existing Resources
Alongside greenﬁeld exploration, GMRICS continues to 
identify opportunities for value addition across GMDC' s 
existing mineral portfolio. Exploration at Kadipani has 
enhanced the understanding of ﬂuorite and associated 
metal mineralisation, creating avenues for value addition 
and future development. Exploration across the Gadhsisa 
Group of bauxite mines has identiﬁed bentonite horizons 
and gallium occurrences, opening new possibilities for 
future resource development. Investigations at Rajpardi 
are continuing to enhance the utilisation of glass sand 
resources. In western Kutch, studies have also conﬁrmed 
the potential of limestone at Panandhro Extension, Lakhpat 
Punhrajpur and Bharkandam, particularly for high-value 
pharmaceutical and food-grade applications.Every mine begins with understanding the geology beneath the surface . As GMDC expands its resource portfolio and enters 
new mineral frontiers, the Gujarat Mineral Research & Industrial Consultancy Society (GMRICS) is playing a central role in 
identifying, evaluating and developing the mineral assets that will support the Company' s long-term growth. Revitalised in 
2024, GMRICS combines geological expertise , modern exploration techniques and scientiﬁc research to transform 
geological potential into future mining opportunities. Working across Gujarat' s diverse mineral belts, the organisation is 
systematically strengthening the State's mineral inventory while creating a pipeline of resources that supports India 's 
ambitions in energy security , critical minerals and industrial development.

57Safety at GMDC 
A Culture of Zero Harm
At GMDC, safety is a responsibility that begins before an 
operation starts and extends across every aspect of the 
workplace . It encompasses the way risks are identiﬁed, 
people are trained, equipment is maintained, emergencies 
are anticipated and operations are monitored. As GMDC 
expands across Gujarat and Odisha, opens new mines and 
diversiﬁes into new areas of activity, the Company is 
strengthening its safety systems with equal focus on 
people , processes, technology and scientiﬁc assessment.
At the heart of this approach is GMDC's Zero Harm 
objective . Achieving it requires more than compliance . It 
calls for collective ownership , open reporting, rigorous risk 
assessment and continuous learning, with employees and 
business partners actively participating in hazard 
identiﬁcation and preventive action.
GMDC' s safety framework is supported by recognised 
occupational health and safety standards and regulatory 
requirements, including ISO 45001:2018, Directorate 
General of Mines Safety (DGMS) safety practices and the 
regulatory framework established under the Mines Act and 
Ministry of Coal requirements.
ISO 45001:2018Occupational Health & Safety certiﬁcation
Safety PracticesAligned with regulatory frameworksSafety and Health Management S ystem (SHMS) A udit 
of Opencast Lignite Mines
A strong safety culture is underpinned by systems that are 
regularly assessed against deﬁned standards. GMDC 
conducted a Safety and Health Management System 
(SHMS) audit across ﬁve opencast lignite mines through an 
expert external agency , in accordance with the guidelines 
circulated by the Ministry of Coal. The audit assessed the 
maturity of safety management processes at each mine site 
and benchmarked them against national standards for 
occupational health and safety in coal and lignite mining. 
The exercise provided a structured assessment of the 
safety management practices followed across the mines, 
helping identify areas for continued strengthening and 
improvement. It reinforces GMDC's approach of 
systematically reviewing safety systems and ensuring that 
they continue to evolve with the Company' s operational 
requirements.
=== page 59 ===
Safety and Health Management S ystem (SHMS) A udit 
Training
Strengthening safety systems also requires building the 
internal capability to understand, implement and sustain 
them. In line with GMDC's commitment to enhancing 
workplace safety and health standards, a six-day training 
programme on SHMS Audit methodology was conducted 
by a distinguished professor from the Indian Institute of 
Technology (IIT) Kharagpur , in accordance with Ministry of 
Coal guidelines. The programme brought together safety 
oﬃcers, mine managers and key personnel from various 
project sites. It strengthened their understanding of SHMS 
guidelines, audit methodology and audit procedures while 
building internal capability to conduct and sustain future 
audits. Together , the external SHMS audit and the internal 
training programme strengthen both sides of the safety 
framework: independent assessment of existing systems 
and internal capability to continuously improve them.
Building a Safety-Conscious Workforce
A safer workplace begins with people who understand the 
risks associated with their work and know how to respond 
to them. GMDC continues to invest in specialised training 
across supervisory , technical and frontline roles while 
strengthening employee health, emergency preparedness 
and safety awareness.
GMDC proactively organises comprehensive medical 
examinations, skill-enhancement vocational training 
sessions and critical ﬁrst-aid and ﬁreﬁghting workshops to 
safeguard employee well-being and foster a culture of 
safety awareness, resilience and emergency 
preparedness across operational sites.
During the year 1,493 employees at GMDC' s Lignite Mines 
underwent annual medical examinations, while 1,198 
employees participated in vocational training, reaﬃrming 
GMDC's commitment to employee health, safety and 
continuous skill development.
At GMDC' s Metal Mines, 56 employees underwent annual 
medical examinations and 76 employees participated in 
vocational training, reﬂecting the Company' s focus on 
workforce well-being, competency enhancement and safe 
mining practices.Safety awareness is reinforced through structured 
campaigns and workforce engagement. During the year, 
GMDC observed the 26th Gujarat Lignite Mines Safety & 
Swachhata Week and the 14th Gujarat Metalliferous Mines 
Safety , Swachhata & Silicosis Awareness Week, bringing 
greater attention to occupational hazards, workplace 
cleanliness and employee well-being.
The Company also conducted regular medical check -ups, 
emergency preparedness drills and ﬁreﬁghting workshops, 
equipping employees with essential skills to recognise 
risks and respond eﬀectively .
Workman Inspector & Structural Supervisor Training
Frontline supervision plays a critical role in translating 
safety systems into safe practices at the workplace . A 
dedicated Workman Inspector and Structural Supervisor 
training session was organised at iCEM, covering essential 
topics related to mine safety and the responsibilities of 
inspectors and supervisors.
The programme reinforced the front-line accountability 
structure that underpins GMDC's safety management 
system and strengthened the capability of those 
responsible for inspection, supervision and day-to-day 
safety oversight.

Engineering Safer Operations
People and processes are supported by engineering and 
operational controls designed to identify and manage risks 
at source . GMDC continues to strengthen these controls 
across its mines through scientiﬁc assessment, real-time 
monitoring and preventive intervention.Tool Box Talks: Embedding Safety in Daily Operations
Safety is most eﬀective when it is built into the routine of 
every shift. At GMDC, Tool Box Talks (TBT) are a vital part of 
daily safety practice , fostering proactive hazard awareness 
and preventive action. These short, focussed discussions 
are conducted at the start of each shift and are led by site 
supervisors, safety oﬃcers or workmen inspectors. They 
bring safety communication directly to the point of work, 
helping employees and workmen understand the hazards 
associated with the day's activities and the precautions 
required before work begins.
By making safety communication a part of every shift, Tool 
Box Talks reinforce the principle that prevention begins 
with awareness at the workplace itself .

Restoring Landscapes. Reviving Ecosystems. Building a 
Greener Legacy .
At GMDC, environmental responsibility begins with 
recognising that mining is a temporary intervention in a 
landscape and that the land, water and ecosystems around 
it must have a future beyond mining. Our approach 
therefore extends across the entire mining lifecycle , from 
scientiﬁc mine planning and progressive reclamation to 
aﬀorestation, biodiversity conservation, water 
stewardship , waste management and clean energy . Over 
the past two decades, GMDC has reclaimed more than 
1,300 hectares of mined-out and overburdened land 
through sustained aﬀorestation, with a focus on native and 
carbon-sequestering species.
Restoring Landscapes
GMDC' s reclamation philosophy is centred on restoring 
ecological function rather than simply returning land to its 
original form. Overburden is reused for backﬁlling and 
biological reclamation, while mined-out areas are 
progressively transformed into greenbelts, grasslands, 
agroforestry plots and water bodies. At Tadkeshwar, 
collaboration with the Forest Department and local 
communities has transformed external dumps into the 
green Vad Garden, supported by scientiﬁcally designed 
slopes, drainage systems and coir-based geotextiles for 
erosion control.
The Company' s Project Hariyali Vann, Sanjeevini Vann and 
Project Navjivan Vann initiatives further extend this 
approach. At Umarsar, Navjivan Vann is creating a 
25-hectare green landscape with 60,000 saplings across 
10 native species and Under the Sanjeevani Van initiative , 
33,100 saplings have been planted across 21 hectares of land. Across Umarsar and Mata no Madh, more than 2.40 
lakh saplings were dispersed through seed-ball 
distribution between FY 2021-22 and FY 2025-26, using an 
in-house rotary drum method timed with the monsoon.
GMDC has also developed agroforestry pilots at Mothala-
Balachod and Naredi-II, where mango trees and fruit 
orchards are being nurtured using treated mine water . A 
5,000 sq ft nursery with a capacity of 20,000 saplings 
supports plantation programmes while serving as a live 
demonstration of biodiversity-led restoration.
At LTPS, the environmental programme includes a mini 
biodiversity forest featuring 20 native species, alongside 
plantation of 250 Kesar mango trees at the LTPS Colony . 
GMDC has set an annual target of planting 10,000 trees, 
strengthening green cover and ecological resilience in the 
Kutch region.
Biodiversity That R eturns With The Green Cover
Reclamation is being designed to create habitats rather 
than merely green spaces. Native species such as Desi 
Babool, Khijda, Kher , Neem, Banyan and Bamboo are being 
prioritised for their ecological suitability and carbon-
sequestering potential. Gouchar grasslands, bird feeders, 
small ponds and earthen watering pots are being 
incorporated into reclaimed landscapes, creating habitats 
that support returning wildlife including leopards, chinkaras 
and migratory birds.
The Company' s commitment to biodiversity also extends to 
productive landscapes. Mango , custard apple , dragon fruit, 
banana and chikoo plantations demonstrate how 
reclaimed and treated land can support both ecological 
restoration and productive use.Enabling Responsible Growth
Growth, for GMDC, is about creating value that reaches far beyond the resources we develop. It is about nurturing the 
land, strengthening communities, enabling our people and building trust through every action we take. From greener 
landscapes and stronger livelihoods to safer workplaces, continuous learning and transparent governance, every eﬀort 
contributes to a future where people, progress and the planet grow together .

61Enabling Environmental Stewardship
=== page 63 ===
Water: 
From Mined-out Pits T o Community Assets
Water stewardship is particularly important across GMDC' s 
operations in water-stressed regions such as Kutch. Mined 
out pits are being repurposed as reservoirs, with monsoon 
runoﬀ harvested through pit catchments and sediment 
control systems. During FY 2025-26, rainwater harvesting 
ponds at Mata no Madh and Mevasa provided capacities of 
appro ximately 3,00,197 kL and 1,73,000 kL respectively for 
freshwater utilisation. The harvested water is used for 
activities including dust suppression and plantation, 
reducing dependence on freshwater sources.
GMDC has also strengthened treatment and reuse 
infrastructure through pH-neutralisation systems, Eﬄuent 
Treatment Plants and a 250 KLD mobile RO unit capable of 
treating water with TDS levels of up to 35,000 ppm. Treated 
water is reused for horticulture , domestic requirements and 
CSR initiatives. A 25 KLD sewage treatment plant is also 
being installed for greywater recycling. Drip irrigation, area-
wise watering schedules, garland drains and siltation 
ponds further improve water-use eﬃciency and reduce 
runoﬀ and sedimentation.
Beyond the mine boundary , GMDC' s water stewardship 
extends to communities through check dams, overhead 
tanks and village ponds supporting agricultural and 
household water needs.
Cleaner Energy , Lower Emissions
GMDC is progressively integrating renewable energy into 
its operations. The Company operates 201 MW of wind 
power across Gujarat and a 5 MW solar plant developed on 
reclaimed mined-out land. During FY 2025-26, the solar 
plant generated approximately 6.4 million units, 
contributing to an estimated reduction of 6,208 tonnes of 
CO₂, while the wind portfolio generated 327.1 MU, 
corresponding to an estimated reduction of appro ximately 
3,32, 128 tonnes of CO₂.
Operational measures also include a 60-metre fog cannon 
for airborne dust suppression and new ETP and RO 
facilities for the treatment and reuse of acidic mine water .
Scientiﬁc Mine Closure
For GMDC, mine closure is planned as an integral part of 
the mining lifecycle rather than an activity reserved for the 
end of operations. Progressive closure is undertaken in 
accordance with approved, submitted and prepared mine 
closure plans and applicable guidelines of the Ministry of 
Coal and Indian Bureau of Mines. Financial provisions and 
progressive closure expenditure are tracked to ensure that 
restoration progresses alongside mining.
As of 31 March 2026, mine closure provision of `781.69 
crore and `56.03 for the progressive mine closure during 
the year FY 26.
Scientiﬁc closure practices encompass backﬁlling, 
landform restoration, slope stabilisation, drainage 
management, biological reclamation, aﬀorestation and 
post-mining land use. The objective is to leave behind 
landscapes that are stable , productive and capable of 
supporting ecological and community needs long after 
extraction has ended.
From Reclamation to Regeneration
Environmental stewardship increasingly extends into how 
reclaimed land can support agriculture and local 
livelihoods. At the Panandhro Lignite Project, GMDC has 
developed a 45-acre Napier grass plot on mined-out land 
supported by Jeevamrut and Biochar applications to 
improve soil quality and fertility. A training and ﬁeld 
programme led by CAZRI scientists introduced farmers to 
Napier cultivation, Jeevamrut, Ghan Jeevamrut, silage 
preparation and biochar applications, connecting land 
restoration with sustainable agricultural practices.
The broader programme included 250 farmers, including 
50 women farmers, strengthening the link between 
environmental restoration, knowledge-sharing and rural 
livelihoods.
GMDC' s environmental journey is therefore not limited to 
reducing the impact of mining. It is about creating a positive 
legacy from the land we work on: forests where mining 
once took place , reservoirs where pits once stood, habitats 
where biodiversity can return and productive landscapes 
that can serve communities for years to come .
Closing The L oop on W aste
GMDC follows structured waste management 
practices across its operations. Overburden is 
reused for backﬁlling and biological reclamation, 
while ﬂy ash is utilised in mine rehabilitation. Used 
oil, biomedical waste , e-waste and battery waste 
are managed through authorised recyclers, 
agencies and supplier take-back programmes, 
supporting responsible disposal and circularity .Enabling Billion Dreams of Viksit Bharat

Materiality Assessment Materiality Matrix
We undertook the materiality assessment in FY 2025, 
enabling eﬀective resource allocation, alignment with our 
sustainability goal and enhance stakeholder value . We 
continue to recognise the material topics derived through 
the assessment process as a cornerstone of our 
sustainability journey It forms an integral part of our 
reporting framework, ensuring focus on the most relevant 
environmental, social and governance aspects while 
upholding transparency in our sustainability practices.GMDC identiﬁed 10 material topics prioritised based on 
their high relevance to both stakeholders and the business. 
These topics constitute the foundation of GMDC’ s long-
term strategic vision and are integral to its operational 
decision-making processes. They are accorded dedicated

GMDC’ s ESG governance framework is anchored in Board-

management systems, functional leadership and 
committee-based monitoring. The Board guides strategy ,

considerations into core business decision-making.
